scenes.heading: Writing an estimate that wins jobs without underpricing

sents.d: Writing an estimate that wins jobs without underpricing
A clear, professional estimate builds trust and protects your margin.
A vague verbal estimate creates room for disputes later — a written estimate specifying exactly what's included, what's excluded, and the total price sets clear expectations before work begins.

Presenting a tiered estimate (a basic option and a more complete option) rather than a single price gives customers a sense of control and can increase average job value when they choose the higher tier.

scenes.heading: Follow up in a few days

sents.d: Following up on estimates that haven't been accepted within a few days, rather than assuming no response means no interest, recovers a meaningful percentage of jobs that would otherwise be lost to simple inaction.

take: Send written, tiered estimates and follow up.
